title: Transient tenant DNS affinity degradation during GPU-pool node swap
text:
Transient tenant DNS affinity degradation during GPU-pool node swap

description:
Two customers reported brief but recurring failures where private tenant hostnames resolved to stale or wrong endpoints immediately after Dedicated GPU pool node swaps (scale-down + rebalance). Users observed 5xxs and short-lived cross-tenant DNS anomalies. This ticket tracks investigation, mitigations, and a deployable fix to guarantee resolver/egress affinity preservation during node handoffs.

steps_to_reproduce:
1) Create a dedicated GPU pool with two nodes and a tenant pinned to node A. 2) Start a workload that establishes long-lived resolver sessions and issues repeated internal hostname lookups. 3) Trigger a scale-down or node drain that causes tenant to migrate to node B. 4) Observe DNS resolution results for private hostnames during and after the handoff window (0-30s).

investigation_notes:
- Correlated customer incident timestamps with node swap events from orchestration (k8s Cordons + custom drain hooks).
- pcap traces show resolver UDP queries forwarded to expected local resolver until a small gap where socket affinity is lost and queries get routed to a resolver from another tenant's ephemeral SNAT mapping.
- Logs show egress-resolver reconciliation completed but without verifying lease ownership on the ephemeral mapping object.
- Rate of occurrence increases during rapid scale-downs where teardown confirmation latencies exceed 1500ms.
- No indications of malicious actor; appears to be a race in allocator + reconcilier during tear-down and reattach.

root_cause:
A race condition in the egress-resolver reconciliation flow: when a node is drained, the ephemeral egress metadata (resolver binding + SNAT port assignment) is torn down asynchronously. If a new tenant attachment is created on a different node before the teardown publishes a tombstone/epoch marker, the allocator can inadvertently reuse the same ephemeral binding, leaving a short window where DNS queries are multiplexed to an address still carrying previous tenant association. The reconciliation did not atomically assert ownership or epoch, allowing stale mappings to be observed by other tenants.

fix_summary:
1) Introduce an epoch-based lease on ephemeral egress bindings and require reconciliation to assert lease id before reusing any binding. 2) Add an explicit tombstone write path on teardown that blocks reuse for N seconds (configurable, default 5s). 3) Harden allocator to prefer creating new bindings rather than reassigning recently released ones when a node swap is detected. 4) Add unit + integration tests and a chaos test that repeatedly drains nodes under load.

rollout_plan:
1) Deploy fix to staging clusters and run dedicated e2e with drain/restore scenarios. 2) Canary rollout to 5% of Dedicated zones (non-critical customers) for 24h while monitoring DNS miss/5xx rate. 3) Expand to 50% for 6h, then 100% if no regressions. 4) Automated rollback if DNS errors exceed baseline + 2 sigma for 10m. 5) Backfill fix to older runtime-1.21 line for customers on pinned releases.

qa_steps:
- Run reproducible drain test harness (script attached in links) for 500 iterative drains across varying concurrency.
- Validate that for each drain, no cross-tenant DNS resolution is observed in pcap and that ephemeral binding reuse count stays at 0 during the reserved window.
- Load test tenant traffic to validate no latency regressions (+/- 5ms target).
- Run integration test with Dedicated autoscaler under synthetic churn to validate stability.

monitoring_and_alerts:
- Add metric: egress_binding_reuse_attempts (counter).
- Add metric: resolver_cross_tenant_failures (counter by tenant).
- Dashboard: DNS resolution success rate and 5xx count for Dedicated nodes over 1m/5m windows.
- Pager alert: resolver_cross_tenant_failures > 1 for any single tenant in 5m.
- Post-deploy runbook to toggle tombstone window if false positives observed.

follow_up_tasks:
Create long-term allocator perf optimization spike (ENG-xxxxxx)
Audit all teardown paths for tombstone semantics
Document troubleshooting steps in Console KB

notes:
Customer communication drafted: notify affected customers (Acme Health, FinBridge Labs) with timeline and mitigation. Support already applied temporary mitigation by pinning affected tenants to a stable node and increasing drain grace period. Final postmortem to be posted to Confluence with traffic graphs and packet captures.
